reasons: The rule's preferred position requires a 12-month conformance period for software; p0077 grants only ninety days for Deliverables, which (per the Section 1.4 definition covering configurations, integrations, designs and workflows) is software work product, so classifying this as a duration deviation is defensible.

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position: it changes only the period in 19.2 ('ninety days' → 'twelve (12) months') and leaves the Hosted Services term, authority warranty, and the 19.4 remedy intact. Direction is customer-favorable.

The remaining preferred elements are already satisfied in the surrounding text (19.1 professional/workmanlike and conformance; 19.3 compliance with law and no malicious code; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace plus termination and refund; 19.5 disclaimer limited to implied warranties and expressly preserving express warranties and remedies), so no further operations are required for rule completeness.
The comment accurately describes the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (express ninety (90) days with 19.4 untouched) without lecturing; tone and prefix conform.

Deterministic checks are consistent: the period remains ≥ 90 days and is expressed in months, and the 0.319 changed-character ratio reflects a single-phrase substitution within a short clause rather than an over-broad rewrite.
